question.problem:
Suppose we take a random sample of size $n=125$ from a population where $75%$ of the population has a particular characteristic. Find a normal approximation for the probability that more than $65%$ but less than $72%$ of the sample has the characteristic. You may assume that the population size is significantly larger than the sample size. *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.05\,$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$
$\,-0.7\,$ $\,0.2266\,$ $\,0.2236\,$ $\,0.2206\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2578\,$ $\,0.2546\,$ $\,0.2514\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.2912\,$ $\,0.2877\,$ $\,0.2843\,$
$z$$\,0.06\,$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$
$\,-2.5\,$ $\,0.0052\,$ $\,0.0051\,$ $\,0.0049\,$
$\,-2.4\,$ $\,0.0069\,$ $\,0.0068\,$ $\,0.0066\,$
$\,-2.3\,$ $\,0.0091\,$ $\,0.0089\,$ $\,0.0087\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a population in which a proportion $p$ of the population has a particular characteristic, the sampling distribution of the sample proportion $\overset{^}{\,p}$ can be approximated as

$$
\overset{^}{\,p}∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}),
$$

where the sample size $n$ is much smaller than the population size, $np>5,$ and $n(1-p)>5.$

In our case

- the sample size is $n=125,$ and

- the population proportion is $p=0.75.$

Now, since

$$
np=125(0.75)=93.75>5
$$

and

$$
n(1-p)=125(1-0.75)=31.25>5,
$$

and $n=125$ is much smaller than the population size, we can apply the above approximation.

The sampling distribution of the sample proportion, in this case, can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{^}{\,p} & ∼N(p,\frac{p(1-p)}{n}) \\  & ∼N(0.75,\frac{0.75(1-0.75)}{125}) \\  & ∼N(0.75,0.0015).\end{aligned}
$$

The probability we wish to find is
$P(0.65<\overset{^}{\,p}\le 0.72).$
So, we convert $\overset{^}{\,p}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.65<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.72) & =P(\frac{0.65-0.75}{\sqrt{0.0015}}<Z\le \frac{0.72-0.75}{\sqrt{0.0015}}) \\  & ≈P(-2.58<Z\le -0.77) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.77)-P(Z\le -2.58) \\  & =Φ(-0.77)-Φ(-2.58)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.77) & =0.2206 \\ Φ(-2.58) & =0.0049.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.65<\overset{^}{\,p}<0.72) & =Φ(-0.77)-Φ(-2.58) \\  & =0.2206-0.0049 \\  & =0.2157.\end{aligned}
$$
